Pechenegs: Extinct Turkic people. The Pechenegs or Patzinaks, were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who spoke the Pecheneg language.
Serving as the 64th Bishop of Rome from 590 until 604, this former Roman prefect sent missionaries to England, including Augustine of Canterbury — who was he?
Pope Gregory I: 64th Bishop of Rome; head of the Roman Catholic Church from AD 590 to 604.
In October 2021, this U.S. assistant secretary for health became the nation's first openly transgender four-star officer across all eight uniformed services — who is she?
Rachel Levine: American public health official (born 1957)

This short-lived 1990s state in the Balkans seceded from a disintegrating Yugoslavia in 1992, triggering a three-year war as rival Serb and Croat factions carved out their own unrecognized quasi-states — what state?
Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Balkan country (1992–1995)

A vocal critic of the Federal Reserve and mass surveillance programs, this Texas congressman ran for president as the Libertarian nominee in 1988 before seeking the Republican nomination twice more — who is he?

In 1982 this child from Manchester, Maine wrote a letter to Soviet leader Yuri Andropov — and got a personal reply inviting her to visit the USSR, making her 'America's Youngest Ambassador' — who was she?
Samantha Smith: American child peace activist (1972–1985)
Once a commander of Alexander the Great's elite infantry, this Macedonian general later ruled Asia Minor, Syria, Mesopotamia, and Iran, founding an empire that bore his name — who was he?
Seleucus I Nicator: Macedonian general, Diadochus, and founder of the Seleucid Empire.
Spanning Emperor Hirohito's reign from 1926 to 1989, this period saw Japan's wartime totalitarian turn, defeat in World War II, and a nearly seven-year American-led occupation — which era?
Shōwa era: Period of Japanese history (1926–1989)
Based on the island of Sumatra, this maritime empire became a key center for spreading Buddhism across Southeast Asia between the 7th and 11th centuries — which empire?
Srivijaya: Empire based on Sumatra (c. 671–1025 AD)
A military engineer who is a national hero in Poland, Lithuania, Belarus AND the United States, he fought for the American Revolution before leading an uprising in 1794 — who was he?
This centrist political position blends economically liberal ideas with social democratic policy, favoring workfare over welfare — what's it called?
Third Way: Centrist political position. The Third Way has been promoted by social liberal and social-democratic parties.
A law professor with a doctorate from the London School of Economics, she became the first woman to serve as president of the Republic of China, from 2016 to 2024 — who is she?

Tsai Ing-wen: President of the Republic of China from 2016 to 2024. Following the DPP's defeat in the 2008 presidential election, Tsai was elected party chair, a position she held three times (2008–2012, 2014–2018, and 2020–2022).

This King of Italy also claimed the titles Emperor of Ethiopia and King of the Albanians after Italy's invasions of those countries, and reigned through the entire rise and fall of the Fascist regime — who was he?
Victor Emmanuel III: King of Italy from 1900 to 1946.
Nicknamed the "Land Cruiser War," this conflict erupted in Sudan in 2003 and led to President Omar al-Bashir being indicted for genocide by the International Criminal Court. What was it?
War in Darfur: Genocidal conflict in Western Sudan.
Also known as the Prince of Orange, he led the Dutch revolt against Spanish Habsburg rule that ignited the Eighty Years' War and eventually won the United Provinces their independence — who is he?
William the Silent: Dutch revolt leader (1533–1584)

Born to a family of strawberry farmers in Akita Prefecture, this politician rose to become Japan's Prime Minister from 2020 to 2021 after years as Chief Cabinet Secretary under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Yoshihide Suga: Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021. Yoshihide Suga (菅 義偉, Suga Yoshihide; born 6 December 1948) is a Japanese former politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021.
Which one below was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four. Thomas Carlyle (4 December 1795 – 5 February 1881) was a Scottish essayist, historian and philosopher.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four. C++ is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Danish computer scientist Bjarne Stroustrup.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Which of these is a mathematician?
Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Uranium?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
What is the atomic number of Vanadium?
Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
In what year was Jimmy Wales born?
Jimmy Wales: Jimmy Donal Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.
In what year was Mikhail Mishustin born?
Mikhail Mishustin: Mikhail Vladimirovich Mishustin (born 3 March 1966) is a Russian politician and economist serving as the prime minister of Russia since 2020.
In what year was Thomas Edison born?
Thomas Edison: Thomas Alva Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
In what year did Alfred Nobel die?
Alfred Nobel: Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
In what year did Leonhard Euler die?
Leonhard Euler: Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
In what year was Methylphenidate discovered?
Methylphenidate: It may be taken by mouth or applied to the skin, and different formulations have varying durations of effect.
Which company manufactures TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish Aerospace Industries. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Chromium: Pfizer. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In which country did the Hawker Siddeley Harrier take place?
Hawker Siddeley Harrier: United Kingdom. The Hawker Siddeley Harrier is a British jet-powered attack aircraft designed and produced by the British aerospace company Hawker Siddeley.
Who is credited with discovering Meitnerium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Meitnerium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
Who is credited with discovering Allergic rhinitis?
Allergic rhinitis: John Bostock. It is classified as a type I hypersensitivity reaction.
Who is credited with discovering SARS-CoV-2?
SARS-CoV-2: Zhang Jixian. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Roughly two-thirds of the 150,000 people who die each day succumb to causes linked to this gradual, damage-driven process of growing older — what is it?
Ageing (or aging in American English) is the process of becoming older.
In this group of diseases, misfolded proteins clump into fibrils and accumulate in body tissue, sometimes causing an enlarged tongue or carpal tunnel syndrome — name the condition?
Amyloidosis is a group of diseases in which abnormal proteins, known as amyloid fibrils, build up in tissue.
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
Formed naturally through evaporation of saline water or generated by salt mining, which concentrated saltwater solution helps de-ice roads and preserve pickled foods?
Brine (or briny water) is a high-concentration solution of salt (typically sodium chloride or calcium chloride) in water.
Chili peppers likely make this hydrophobic compound to deter hungry mammals and fungi — yet it's exactly what gives them their burning, pungent heat. What is it?
Capsaicin (8-methyl-N-vanillyl-6-nonenamide) (commonly) is a toxin that is the main active component of chili peppers and gives them their distinct pungent, "spicy" or "hot" taste.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Whose larvae track down plant roots to eat by sensing both leaf-released volatiles and carbon dioxide, in a European scarab species also known as the Maybeetle?
Cockchafer (Melolontha melolontha), also colloquially known as the Maybug, Maybeetle, or doodlebug, is a species of scarab beetle belonging to the genus Melolontha.
In this satirical action comedy, a group of self-absorbed actors filming a war movie are dropped in the jungle by their fed-up director and must rely on real survival skills. What film is it?
Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
This genus of roughly 340 species includes the carnation and the sweet william, and is nicknamed 'pink' — which genus?

Dianthus (dy-) is a genus of about 340 species of flowering plants in the family Caryophyllaceae, native mainly to Europe and Asia, with a few species in northern and southern Africa, and one species (D. repens) in arctic North America.
Trained in both mathematics and philosophy, which Austrian-German thinker developed the concept of phenomenological reduction and founded a major 20th-century school of philosophy?
Edmund Husserl (Austrian; 8 April 1859 - 27 April 1938) was an Austrian-German philosopher and mathematician who established the school of phenomenology.
This class of mental health condition is defined by an enduring, pervasive pattern of behavior, emotion, and thought that deviates from social norms and develops early in life. What is it?
Erythritol is an organic compound, the naturally occurring achiral meso four-carbon sugar alcohol (or polyol).

This Arabic term describes the human interpretation and practice of Islamic religious law, expanded through jurists' scholarly reasoning and expressed in the rulings they issue on questions of faith. What is this field called?
Fiqh is the term for Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
Also called the woodchuck, this North American rodent is exceptional among its kin: while most marmots live in rocky mountains, this lowland burrower roams the Eastern U.S. into Alaska — what is it?
Groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.
A member of the human Herpesviridae family, this contagious pathogen comes in two types, with about 67% of people under 50 carrying the first as of 2016. What is it?
Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1 and HSV-2) are two members of the human Herpesviridae family, a set of viruses that produce viral infections in the majority of humans.
Defined by Whipple's triad, this condition occurs when blood sugar falls below about 70 mg/dL, causing symptoms like headache, shakiness, confusion, and a fast heart rate — what's it called?

Hypoglycemia (American English), also spelled hypoglycaemia or hypoglycmia (British English), sometimes called low blood sugar, is a fall in blood sugar to levels below normal, typically below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L).
Widely planted outside its native South America for its striking purple flowers, this tree is considered Vulnerable in the wild according to the IUCN — which species?
Jacaranda mimosifolia is a sub-tropical tree native to south-central South America that has been widely planted elsewhere because of its attractive and long-lasting violet-colored flowers.
While tinkering with electromagnets, which American physicist discovered self-inductance and later became the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution?
Joseph Henry (December 17, 1797- May 13, 1878) was an American physicist and inventor who served as the first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.

Sold under a well-known brand name, this medication treats several types of epilepsy including focal and tonic-clonic seizures, and also helps stabilize mood by reducing future depressive episodes in bipolar disorder — which drug?
Lamotrigine (luh-), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
Named from the Greek word for 'stone,' this alkali metal with symbol Li tarnishes from silver to black in air and was once mined mainly from pegmatite minerals — what is it?
Lithium (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 32 to 57 deciduous trees and shrubs in the rose family includes the ancestors of a familiar orchard fruit plus ornamental wild and crab varieties — what's the genus?
Malus (or) is a genus of about 32-57 species of small deciduous trees or shrubs in the family Rosaceae, including the domesticated orchard apple, crab apples, and wild apples.
More than 80% of cases trace to asbestos exposure, and it grows from the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — which cancer is it?
Mesothelioma is a type of cancer that develops from the thin layer of tissue that covers many of the internal organs (known as the mesothelium).
This unique group of mammals is the only one whose members lay eggs rather than bear live young, comprising the platypus and four echidna species — what group is it?
Monotreme are mammals of the order Monotremata.

Encompassing several types of kidney inflammation affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or nearby interstitial tissue, this general medical term falls under the broader category of nephropathy — what's the condition?
Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys and may involve the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue surrounding the glomeruli and tubules.
This Persian polymath and poet was the first to provide a general geometric solution to all third-degree polynomial equations, using the intersection of conic sections. Who is he?
Omar Khayyam (1048-1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
This galliform game bird, native to Europe, Asia, and Africa, was once lumped in with pheasants and quail, but DNA suggests it isn't one distinct group at all — which bird is it?
Partridge is a medium-sized galliform bird in any of several genera, with a wide native distribution throughout parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.
Found in more than 200 species of mushroom, this inactive compound is a prodrug your body quickly converts to psilocin, a near-cousin of serotonin — what is it?
Psilocybin (4-), is a naturally occurring tryptamine alkaloid and investigational drug found in more than 200 species of mushrooms, with hallucinogenic and serotonergic effects.
What fat-soluble alcohol form of vitamin A — found in fish, dairy, and meat — is essential for vision, skin maintenance, and immune function, and is used as a supplement to prevent xerophthalmia?
Retinol is a hydrolytic metabolite of retinyl esters belonging to the group of vitamin A1 as an alcohol form.

These lizard-like amphibians, grouped in the order Urodela, keep a tail throughout both their larval and adult life stages — unlike their tailless amphibian cousins the frogs and toads. What animal is it?

Salamander are a group of amphibians typically characterized by their lizard-like appearance, with slender bodies, blunt snouts, short limbs projecting at right angles to the body, and the presence of a tail in both larvae and adults.

Essentially plasma with the clotting factors and cells removed, this pale yellow fluid still carries antibodies, hormones, and electrolytes and is central to typing tests done before a transfusion — what is it?
Serum (blood) is the fluid and solvent component of blood which does not play a role in clotting.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Enhanced by painted scenery and stagecraft like lighting, this live performing art shares its name with the very buildings where its shows are staged — what is it?

Theatre is a collaborative form of performing art that uses live performers, usually actors, to present experiences of a real or imagined event before a live audience in a specific place, often a stage.
Latin for 'three-headed,' this large muscle on the back of the upper arm has three parts, one of which also crosses the shoulder joint — name the muscle?
Triceps (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
First glimpsed in 1892 through tobacco-plant disease and counted as the most numerous biological entity on Earth, this submicroscopic agent can only replicate inside a living cell. What is it?
Virus is a submicroscopic infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.

This unit of time is based on how long Earth takes to complete one full orbit around the Sun, with the precise scientific definition running about 365 days, 5 hours, and 48 minutes — what unit is this?

Year is a unit of time based on how long it takes the Earth to orbit the Sun. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Native to North America but now invasive across Europe after being introduced, this semiaquatic mustelid preys on rodents, fish, and frogs — which animal?
American mink: Semiaquatic species of mustelid. Because of range expansion, the American mink is classed as a least-concern species by the IUCN.
Nicknamed "the heart of the scorpion," this reddish supergiant is the brightest star in its constellation — what is it?
Antares: Binary star in the constellation Scorpius.
Sold under the brand name Abilify, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia, bipolar mania, and irritability linked to autism spectrum disorder — what is it?
Aripiprazole: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Aripiprazole is taken by mouth or via injection into a muscle.
Native to the Americas and prized for thousands of years for its unusually oily fruit, this evergreen of the laurel family bears what's botanically a giant berry around a single seed — what is it?
Avocado: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family.
Sometimes called the common, lawn, or English variety, this European plant is considered the archetypal member of the daisy family — what's its scientific name?

Bellis perennis: Species of plant in the daisy family. Bellis perennis ( BEL-iss pə-REN-iss), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
This medical term for blood escaping the circulatory system describes a healthy person as able to lose 10 to 15 percent of their total volume without serious harm — what is it called?
Bleeding: Blood escaping from the circulatory system. Bleeding, hemorrhage, haemorrhage or blood loss, is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.
Making up just 2.6 percent of the brain's weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and houses all ten pairs of cranial nerve origins — what is it?
Brainstem: Posterior part of the brain, adjoining and structurally continuous.
Its Latin name means "chisel-bearing," a nod to the stout egg-laying organs of its members — which insect suborder includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera: Suborder of insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
A founder of humanistic psychology, this American psychologist pioneered person-centered therapy, an approach that also shaped student-centered learning in education — who is he?
Certified in 1984 and developed into a freighter variant for FedEx, this single-engine turboprop utility plane typically seats nine and can be fitted with floats or skis — which aircraft?
Cessna 208 Caravan: Family of utility transport aircraft.
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Triggered by an abnormal immune response to gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye, this chronic autoimmune condition mainly affects the small intestine and often causes malabsorption in children — which condition?
Coeliac disease: Autoimmune disorder. Coeliac disease (Commonwealth English) or celiac disease (American English) is a chronic autoimmune disease, mainly affecting the small intestine.
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Despite its name, this South American freshwater fish is actually a knifefish, not a true eel, and produces powerful discharges using specialized tissue — which species?
Electrophorus electricus: South American electric fish. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Sporting an orange-red breast rimmed in grey and brown upperparts, this small insect-eating songbird ranges from Western Siberia to North Africa — which bird?
European robin: Species of bird. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
The largest region of the brain's cerebral hemispheres, this most-forward area contains the primary motor cortex and is separated from the parietal and temporal regions by two grooves — what is it?
Frontal lobe: Part of the brain. The most anterior ventral, orbital end of the frontal lobe is known as the frontal pole, which is one of the three so-called poles of the cerebrum.
First described by J. D. Hooker in 1889 and nicknamed the Transvaal or Barberton daisy for its South African origins, what genus of flowering plant is this?
Gerbera: Genus of plants. Gerbera ( JUR-bər-ə or GUR-bər-ə) L. is a genus of plants in the Asteraceae (Compositae) family.
This cluster of immune cells forms around bacteria, fungi, or foreign material the body can't otherwise clear away — what is it called?
Granuloma: Inflammatory aggregation of immune cells.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Using only a triangle's three side lengths and their semiperimeter, this ancient geometric method computes the triangle's area — what is it known as?
Heron's formula: Triangle area in terms of side lengths.
Generally colourless, hydrophobic, and faintly gasoline-scented, which organic compound is made entirely of hydrogen and carbon and includes everything from methane to paraffin wax?

Hydrocarbon: Organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon. In the fossil fuel industries, hydrocarbon refers to naturally occurring petroleum, natural gas and coal, or their hydrocarbon derivatives and purified forms.
Designed in 1967 to replace the An-12 and haul heavy machinery into remote, poorly served regions, this four-engine Soviet airlifter earned the NATO name 'Candid' — what is it?
Ilyushin Il-76: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it has a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell or punch straight through a skull between the ears — which animal?
Jaguar: Large cat native to the Americas.
Trained originally in mathematics at Cambridge, this English economist's Depression-era writings became the foundation for a whole school of macroeconomic thought bearing his name — who is he?
This classical physics model imagines matter as countless invisible particles in constant, random collisions, explaining pressure, temperature and viscosity alike — what is it?
Kinetic theory of gases: Understanding of gas properties in terms of molecular motion.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Defined as exactly one cubic decimetre and rooted in an old French unit called the litron, what metric measure of volume is this?
Litre: Unit of volume. The litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used: ℓ) is a metric unit of volume.
A Russian linguist by training, this woman served two separate terms as first lady of Russia, from 2000 to 2008 and again from 2012 to 2014 — who is she?
Lyudmila Putina: Ex-wife of Vladimir Putin (born 1958)
Prized for its sweet, pine-and-citrus flavor, this perennial herb is often considered synonymous with oregano in parts of the Middle East — what is it?
Marjoram: Perennial herb. It is also called pot marjoram, although this name is also used for other cultivated species of Origanum.
Also nicknamed 'Cornish salmon,' this predatory fish is often netted alongside the Atlantic herring it preys on, and is heavily overfished across European waters — which fish?
Merluccius merluccius: Species of fish. Merluccius merluccius or the European hake is a merluccid hake of the genus Merluccius.

Codenamed 'Havoc' by NATO, this Soviet tandem-seat attack helicopter carries a single gun in an under-nose barbette and, unlike its predecessor, has no secondary troop-transport role. What aircraft is this?
Mil Mi-28: Russian attack helicopter. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.

This Japanese biologist used diffusion equations to calculate how likely a gene is to take over a population, and in 1968 proposed the "neutral theory" that genetic drift, not just selection, drives molecular evolution — who was he?
First identified from an 1856 fossil in a German valley, this group of archaic humans roamed Europe and Asia until vanishing around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived — who were they?

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.

The world's most widespread and commercially important cactus species, this domesticated crop is grown both as a fruit and for its edible vegetable pads, likely originating in central Mexico — which species?
Opuntia ficus-indica: Species of cactus. It is grown primarily as a fruit crop, and also for the vegetable nopales and other uses.
One researcher catalogued as many as 549 varieties of this psychological category, defined by intense arousal toward things that aren't sexual by nature — what is the term?
This order of hoofed mammals — horses, rhinos, and tapirs — bears its weight on an odd number of toes and digests plant fiber in its intestines rather than a multi-chambered stomach. Which order?
Perissodactyla: Order of hoofed mammals. Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek περισσός, perissós 'odd' and δάκτυλος, dáktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.

This French polymath's five-volume 'Celestial Mechanics' recast Newtonian physics in the language of calculus, and he pioneered both a widely used integral transform and helped shape Bayesian probability — who is he?
This plant genus — whose members go by names like poplar, aspen, and cottonwood — includes the first tree species ever to have its complete genome sequenced, in 2006 — what genus is it?
Populus: Genus of plants. Populus is a genus of 25–30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
